anf_compare.notes: No published English was consulted; translated from the PG 76 Greek only.

bible_refs.method: wording: 'ἀρχιερέα καὶ ἀπόστολον τῆς ὁμολογίας ἡμῶν … Ἰησοῦν, πιστὸν ὄντα τῷ ποιήσαντι'
bible_refs.note: Order of the two titles reversed; ἑαυτόν for αὐτόν. Paraphrase inside Nestorius' sentence, so not in quotation marks.

bible_refs.method: allusion: offering 'for himself as for the people'
bible_refs.note: Hebrews 5:3 says the high priest offers for the people and for himself; Nestorius applies it to Jesus.
Cited with 5:3, since 7:27 alone says Christ had no need to offer for himself.
The quotation continues at the start of dial-rem-close.

choices.why: The Nicene term; kept the same in both speakers' mouths so the argument turns on one word.

choices.english: God is inseparable from the one who is seen
choices.why: ἀχώριστος is an adjective of possibility ('that cannot be separated'); 'inseparable' keeps that force. τοῦ φαινομένου is the visible man.
rejected: God is not separated from the one who appears

choices.why: θεοπρεπής means befitting God; 'worthy of God' is the natural English.
Two distinct nouns in Nestorius' sentence, kept distinct.

pass_a_gloss: [continuing 'so' from dial-rem-early] also the Virgin, befitting God (θεοπρεπής), bore in flesh God the Word from God. [NESTORIUS] Every mother bears what is of one substance (ὁμοούσιον) with her; so she is not his mother unless he himself exists of one substance with her; for how is she his mother when he exists foreign to her substance (οὐσίας)? [bracketed editor's variant, same sense] [CYRIL] We were taught to confess one Son from the Virgin and from the Holy Spirit, of one substance with the mother as with the Father, just as the Fathers have said. [NESTORIUS] I divide the natures (φύσεις), I unite the worship (προσκύνησιν), since God is inseparable (ἀχώριστος) from the one who appears; for this reason I do not separate the honor (τιμήν). [CYRIL] The one who divides the natures speaks of two sons, not believing the Scripture which says: The Word became flesh. [NESTORIUS] Paul says that Jesus became high priest and apostle of our confession, being faithful to the one who made him; he offered himself as a sacrifice on behalf of himself as on behalf of the people; hence he is appointed high priest in the things toward God. [CYRIL] Paul says: Christ [the quotation of Hebrews 9:28 continues in dial-rem-close]
pass_b_english: …the Virgin too, worthy of God, bore in the flesh God the Word, who is from God.

Nestorius says: Every mother bears what is of one substance with herself. So she is not his mother unless he is of one substance with her. For how is she his mother when he is foreign to her substance?
Cyril says: We have been taught to confess one Son from the Virgin and from the Holy Spirit, of one substance with his mother as he is with the Father, as the Fathers have said.
Nestorius says: I divide the natures, but I unite the worship, since God is inseparable from the one who is seen; for this reason I do not separate the honor.
Cyril says: Whoever divides the natures speaks of two sons, and does not believe the Scripture that says, 'The Word became flesh' (John 1:14).

Nestorius says: Paul says that Jesus became the high priest and apostle of our confession, being faithful to the one who made him (Hebrews 3:1-2), and that he offered himself as a sacrifice for himself as for the people (Hebrews 5:3; 7:27); hence he is appointed high priest in the things that pertain to God (Hebrews 5:1).

καὶ ἡ θεοπρεπὴς Παρθένος ετεκεν ἐν σαρκὶ τὸν ἐκ Θεοῦ Θεὸν Λόγον. {ΝΕΣΤ.} Πᾶσα
μήτηρ τὸ ὁμοούσιον αὐτῆς τίκτει· οὐκ εστιν ουν αὐτοῦ μήτηρ, εἰ μὴ αὐτὸς ὁμοούσιος
αὐτῆς ὑπάρχει· πῶς γὰρ αὐτοῦ μήτηρ τοῦ ἀλλοτρίου τῆς οὐσίας αὐτῆς ὑπάρχοντος
[ξοδ. τὸ ἀλλότριον ὑπάρχον]; {ΚΥΡ.} ̔Ημᾶς ἐκ Παρθένου καὶ ἐκ Πνεύματος ἁγίου ενα
Υἱὸν ἐδιδάχθημεν ὁμολογεῖν, ὁμοούσιον τῇ μητρὶ ὡς τῷ Πατρὶ, καθὼς οἱ Πατέρες
εἰρήκασιν. {ΝΕΣΤ.} ∆ιαιρῶ τὰς φύσεις, ἑνῶ τὴν προσκύνησιν, ἐπειδὴ ἀχώριστος τοῦ
φαινομένου Θεός· διὰ τοῦτο οὐ χωρίζω τὴν τιμήν. {ΚΥΡ.} ̔Ο διαιρῶν τὰς φύσεις, δύο
υἱοὺς λέγει, μὴ πιστεύων τῇ Γραφῇ λεγούσῃ, οτι ̔Ο Λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο. {ΝΕΣΤ.}
Παῦλος λέγει ἀρχιερέα καὶ ἀπόστολον τῆς ὁμολογίας ἡμῶν γενέσθαι ̓Ιησοῦν, πιστὸν
οντα τῷ ποιήσαντι ἑαυτὸν, θυσίαν ἑαυτὸν προσέφερεν ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ ὡς ὑπὲρ τοῦ
λαοῦ· οθεν ἀρχιερεὺς καθίσταται τὰ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν. {ΚΥΡ.} Παῦλος λέγει· Χριστὸς
